cohort: A 40-year-old woman who developed Lance-Adams syndrome (LAS) secondary to cardiopulmonary arrest (CPA) that occurred after her first cesarean delivery at the age of 26 years.
finding: After 3 years of follow-up with high-frequency deep brain stimulation (DBS), the patient showed 8% and 20% improvements in action and resting myoclonus, respectively, but the therapy applied 14 years after hypoxia-causing LAS was not considered sufficiently beneficial.
mod_finding: The patient's cardiopulmonary arrest (CPA), which led to Lance-Adams syndrome (LAS), occurred after her first cesarean delivery.
